courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: So we want to deploy our app here
as a native app, that is what I'll start with
and for these native apps, I want to have my own icons and my own splashscreen.
Now before we actually add these, let's build our app so that we can open it in Android Studio and
Xcode and prepare it for deployment.
For this, what you can do is you can simply run ng build --prod to build your application
for production with the help of the Angular CLI
and for this command to work, you need to make sure you have the Angular CLI installed globally on
your machine.
Now this will take your web app and build it as it would build any regular normal Angular app which you
don't build as an Ionic app or which you don't plan on publishing
as a native app.
So this is what we'll do now,
let's wait for that to finish because with this finished, you can now run ionic capacitor sync android
and what this will do is will take your build web app and basically copy it into the Android folder
and then you repeat that command for iOS, important,
you can only build for iOS if you are building this on MacOS, on Windows or Linux you can only build
for Android.
Now this simply takes the build web app and also copies it into the iOS and Android folders so
that we can continue there. Side note, you can always go into that capacitor-config.json file and adjust
your app ID here which should then be picked up
once you do run onic capacitor run or onic capacitors sync.
So this is that unique app identifier which you need to set to deploy your app because this will uniquely
identify your app in the app stores,
so definitely make sure you set this
and as I explained earlier in the course, this should be set to an identifier which looks like a reverse
domain which doesn't have to really exist but which in the end is your unique identifier, which is why
here, you typically use your company or your personal name,
you end with .com or you start with .com therefore and then you have like a descriptor of your
app
and of course that can be whatever you want.
Typically you'd of course not name it
udemycourse.ionicangular but something like michaelcompany.fitnesstrack or 2019 or whatever
your name is.
But that's just a side note,
I will also show you how to adjust it from inside Xcode or Android Studio and that's the next step.
Let's run ionic capacitor open android to open our project in Android Studio and then of course repeat
the same with iOS if you're on a Mac to also open it in Xcode.
Now here's the project in Android Studio and it should automatically have that androidmanifest.xml
file opened here,
you can also open that in Visual Studio code here in the Android folder under app and there in the source
folder, you should find that Android manifest file which is that same file.
Now what you'll notice here for me at least is that the package ID that is used here is indeed not the
one coded or added to this capacitor-config file I showed you.
Well maybe this changes in the future because I think it should
but right now to adjust your app ID for Android, edit it here in the Android manifest file in that
Android folder and set it just as I described it a few seconds ago to that unique identifier formatted
like a URL or a reverse URL. Make sure to adjust that here and you can learn more about that
in the Capacitor documentation, if you scroll down to Android configuration, there you'll also learn that
you should change the app ID here in your Android manifest.
You also learn how you can change your app name here and for that, you go into the resources folder in
the Android folder there and then under values, strings.xml,
here you find your app name and I will name this PairBnB because that's what we're building here
and I'll also name my main activity PairBnB because that is what essentially gets shown in that
task manager for example and I will also update my package name here to match that package name I have
provided here in that capacitor-config file.
So in these three places, I'll set it to my identifier chosen there and also in the Android manifest.
So if I go back up there to the Android manifest, here I also want to use my identifier and you find
most of these steps also described here, the important steps are also mentioned here.
Now with that set up, we should also check our permissions and there,
we already had a look earlier in this course,
you basically describe what your app is allowed to do.
Now we definitely want internet access,
we also want to be able to write to our storage,
we want to be able to get that location, network state should be determined, camera.
We actually don't need to record audio or modify the audio settings, so you should be able to remove
these two permissions
but in the end, you should always check of course with what your app uses and thoroughly test it after
changing the Android manifest. So with that, we prepared Android,
now to also prepare iOS, let me open this up in Xcode,
here I am
and side note, just as you can configure Android here in your project folder, you can also dive into iOS
there in the app app folder and in that app app folder, you'll find the info.plist which is a file where
you can configure a lot of things, like for example your display name of the application which I'll also
name PairBnB here. There also are dynamically injected things though which you should not
overwrite here. Now back in Xcode, here in the open project, you can click on your project here on the
left, there you can also edit the things I just showed you in the configuration, like for example that
display name. Here it also did pick up that identifier specified in the capacitor-config, so no need
to change it here
and before you deploy, you should also set your versions here to a version
that is seen from outside, that version which you should of course change whenever you update your app
and in internal build which you definitely should change. It's not visible to the outside but internally
and in the App Store controls
which version is the most recent version and so on. For Android to go back to that, we have something
similar if you go into that Android folder, there in the app folder, we have that build gradle file where
you also set a version name that is visible to the outside world which you can set to whatever you
want and your internal version which you should also always change whenever you're deploying a new app
version and here, we have another case where we definitely should add our application ID.
So with that, Android is prepared, iOS is prepared and if you want to configure more here, definitely
dive into the official documentation for publishing Android and iOS apps.
I also wanted to show you how to generate these icons right,
so now with the app generally prepared, let's do this next.
